opportunities.title: Second plan-gate question fires on a safety blocker not covered by any documented STOP condition
opportunities.evidence: session cae7b38b: "vendored installer is fresh-install-only, can't safely build v3" triggered a 2nd AskUserQuestion
opportunities.detail: routing.md's autonomy contract promises exactly ONE plan-gate approval, then autonomous to PR, with 5 enumerated STOP conditions. Discovering mid-worktree that the update mechanism itself is unsafe for an irreplaceable LXC service isn't one of the 5, so the session had to invent a second ad hoc gate — the safe call, but unsanctioned by the doc, so it reads as a contract violation rather than a known exit path.
opportunities.proposed_change: Add a 6th sanctioned STOP condition to routing.md: 'update mechanism cannot be verified safe for in-place bump' — re-present the gate instead of treating a second AskUserQuestion as drift.

opportunities.title: Stale/missing reference docs on the installed skill cause repeated failed Read calls
opportunities.evidence: session 5d231e21: "File does not exist" x4 on bridge.md/routing.md/lifecycle-map.md before ls fallback
opportunities.detail: SKILL.md's Quick Reference table cites references/bridge.md, routing.md, lifecycle-map.md, manifest-schema.md, service-picker.md. The archive copy of this repo has all five, but at least one installed/global copy the sessions actually ran against was missing references/ at session time, costing 3-4 wasted Read attempts per occurrence before an ls fallback found the real path.
opportunities.proposed_change: Ensure the skill-sync path (push-to-profile.ps1 / update-skill) keeps references/ in lockstep with SKILL.md, or have the dispatcher ls the references/ dir once up front instead of blind-Reading each named file.

opportunities.title: "Three-perspective" smoke test is only two perspectives in at least one real deploy script
opportunities.evidence: session 5d231e21: deploy script polls P1 (workstation) + P3 (Traefik) only, no P2/DoH leg wired
opportunities.detail: bridge.md unconditionally describes the smoke test as a three-perspective probe (workstation DNS / public DoH / direct-to-Traefik) and calls it "the only acceptance signal." The homarr deploy script in this session structurally has no DoH leg at all — the probe silently ran at 2-of-3 with no flag raised, so a session can't tell the difference between "P2 intentionally N/A" and "P2 just isn't wired."
opportunities.proposed_change: Either wire the missing DoH leg into affected deploy scripts, or require bridge.md's acceptance signal to explicitly report which of the 3 legs ran and why any leg was skipped.

opportunities.title: GHCR tags/list pagination returned a stale 'latest' version before self-correcting
opportunities.evidence: session 5d231e21: GHCR latest reported v1.32.0, real latest was v1.77.2 via Releases
opportunities.detail: The session caught the discrepancy itself and pivoted to GitHub Releases as the authoritative source before the plan gate, so no bad plan was presented to the operator — but relying on the registry tag list first is a known-unreliable path for version resolution.
opportunities.proposed_change: Make GitHub Releases (not GHCR tags/list) the primary version source for the update-service version-delta check, falling back to registry tags only when no Releases API exists.

opportunities.title: grep-wrapped exit-code check produced an ambiguous 'failed: rc=0' requiring a rerun
opportunities.evidence: session 5d231e21: "failed: rc=0" ambiguity, rerun clean to resolve
opportunities.detail: Self-corrected within one extra turn, but piping a command through grep for a status check masks the real exit code and cost an avoidable retry.
opportunities.proposed_change: Check the underlying command's exit code directly in apply-pattern helper scripts instead of through a grep pipe that can report rc=0 for an unrelated reason.

opportunities.title: Breadcrumb lookup still runs after an explicit slug has already resolved the target
opportunities.evidence: session be10d3e2: breadcrumb check run after explicit slug "taxes" already given
opportunities.detail: Harmless — the explicit arg still won — but routing.md's resolution order says tier 1 (explicit arg) should short-circuit tiers 2-3, not run them anyway.
opportunities.proposed_change: Skip the breadcrumb/picker lookup entirely once an explicit slug arg is present, per the documented resolution order.

opportunities.title: Bare invocation with no arg/breadcrumb resolved its target from conversational memory, not the documented 3-tier order
opportunities.evidence: session 9f35dd14: target injected from "its own prior-turn summary" rather than explicit arg/picker
opportunities.detail: routing.md enumerates exactly 3 resolution tiers for a mutating op: explicit arg, breadcrumb, picker. This session had neither, yet proceeded on a slug+action silently inferred from earlier conversation instead of invoking the AskUserQuestion picker required when both named tiers are absent — a 4th, undocumented resolution source for a destructive-capable op.
opportunities.proposed_change: Require the service picker (AskUserQuestion) on any bare invocation with no explicit arg and no breadcrumb, even when a recent turn implies a target — the operator must confirm, not have it inferred silently.

opportunities.title: Same stale-reference-docs failure as update-service, confirming it's systemic
opportunities.evidence: session 9eb6fc97: failed Read calls on bridge.md/lifecycle-map.md/routing.md before ls fallback
opportunities.detail: Identical root cause to upd-2, reproduced under the opbta-update alias in a separate session — rules out a one-off fluke and confirms a sync-timing gap between SKILL.md's Quick Reference promises and the installed references/ directory.
opportunities.proposed_change: Same fix as upd-2 — one fix at the sync/dispatcher level resolves both commands since they share the underlying skill.

opportunities.title: Public-DoH smoke-test leg skipped for an internal-only FQDN with no documented carve-out
opportunities.evidence: session 9f35dd14: "internal-only FQDN, no public DNS record by design" given as reason to skip P2
opportunities.detail: This session reasoned about the skip transparently in its own output, which is good practice, but bridge.md still states the probe as an unconditional three-leg check with no exception for internal-only services — a future session has no documented basis to skip P2 and could either skip it silently or block on it unnecessarily.
opportunities.proposed_change: Codify an explicit internal-only-FQDN carve-out for the P2/DoH leg in bridge.md so this reasoning is contract-sanctioned rather than ad hoc per session.

opportunities.title: Mis-scoped grep matched ~66KB of unrelated docker-inspect output instead of deploy-log markers
opportunities.evidence: session 9f35dd14: grep matched docker inspect JSON (~66KB) instead of deploy-log markers
opportunities.detail: Self-corrected in the next turn, but a tighter log-path/pattern scope would avoid the token-heavy miss entirely.
opportunities.proposed_change: Scope deploy-log greps to the specific log file/line-prefix pattern rather than a broad match that can also catch docker inspect JSON.

opportunities.title: Clean fallback clone placed outside the repo's worktree-isolation convention
opportunities.evidence: session 9f35dd14: clone built as a sibling of C:\development\, not under .worktrees/
opportunities.detail: Transient and cleaned up afterward (low impact), but bridge.md's dirty-checkout fallback (build a clean tag-pinned clone) doesn't specify where that clone should live, and this session put it beside C:\development\ instead of under the repo's own .worktrees/.
opportunities.proposed_change: Have bridge.md's dirty-checkout fallback explicitly require the clean clone to land under the repo's own .worktrees/ (or a scratch subdir there), not a sibling of the development root.

opportunities.title: Read-only diagnostic probes SSH'd directly to the docker host, bypassing the documented double-hop
opportunities.evidence: session 9f35dd14: two read-only probes SSH'd directly to the docker host, not via ac-devops
opportunities.detail: Low severity since these were read-only and the actual mutating apply correctly went through the double-hop via ac-devops, but bridge.md doesn't state whether read-only diagnostic SSH may bypass that pattern, leaving it to session judgment.
opportunities.proposed_change: Clarify in bridge.md / ac-opbta-ops whether read-only diagnostic probes may SSH directly to service hosts, or require the double-hop uniformly for consistency.
